at: This is my house. You go.
alt: In a roofless Mohe doorway in the snow, a small boy with a shaved crown and braids shouts at Yeon, who crouches in front of him grinning.
scene: Low two-shot at a child's eye level, winter dusk in a burned Mohe village on the eastern border. A charred timber doorframe with no roof, snow settling on black ash. The Mohe boy, about nine, shaved crown and two long braids, fur-trimmed coat, plants a stick against the commander's chest and shouts with his whole body, mouth wide, furious and terrified. Yeon Gesomun, twenty-nine, in Goguryeo steel lamellar with red cloth at the collar, crouches on one knee so the stick touches his breastplate, head tilted, grinning, plainly not understanding a word. Behind them a red-bay horse and two blurred soldiers in falling snow. One hard key: the low red-orange of embers still glowing in the ash, catching the boy's cheek and the steel plates; red #d0362f as ember light, never a glow.

alt: A half-built stone wall snakes over winter hills; a levy gang hauls stones while a tall commander walks the top with a plumb line and a small boy follows.
scene: Wide establishing shot, late winter afternoon on the Goguryeo frontier. A half-built dry-stone border wall of grey cut blocks climbs a long brown ridge in one diagonal, scaffold poles and earth ramps along it, snow in the hollows. A levy gang of young farm soldiers in undyed white hemp with wrapped shins hauls stones on carrying frames and A-frame litters, tiny painted shapes. On top of the wall, small in the upper third, Yeon Gesomun walks the course with a plumb line swinging from his fist, a small Mohe boy with braids one step behind him holding the bob in both hands. Huge pale winter sky in granulated wash, one low sun shaft raking the ridge and throwing long shadows from every stone; red Goguryeo pennants on scaffold poles.

alt: At a stable door at dawn, the Mohe boy in oversized gloves holds the bridle of Yeon's red bay while Yeon, in the saddle, laughs down at him.
scene: Low angle at a timber stable door at first light, frost on the packed earth, breath steaming. The Mohe boy, shaved crown and braids, wears leather gloves far too big for him and holds the bridle of a red-bay horse with both hands, looking up, lips just parted on his first word. Yeon Gesomun sits the horse above him in steel lamellar and a dark travelling cloak, head thrown back in a laugh, one gloveless hand reaching down toward the boy's head. An older man in a grey robe and fur hat stands behind in the doorway, half in shadow. One hard key: low cold dawn through the door behind, a small lamp hung on the post warming the boy's face; red #d0362f only in Yeon's collar cloth.

at: The North comes first, on a Khitan horse.
alt: The Northern Commander rides through Pyongyang’s red two-tier gate on a shaggy steppe horse while two gate guards lean together and gossip.
scene: Low three-quarter angle from inside the gate passage of Pyongyang’s red two-tier munru, late winter morning. The Northern Commander, the attached face, weathered and heavy-shouldered, in Goguryeo steel lamellar with red cloth at the collar and a fur mantle, rides through the stone hongye arch on a short shaggy dun steppe horse with a Khitan saddle blanket, looking down at the guards with a flat, bored stare, ring-pommel sword at his hip. In the sharp dark foreground two gate guards with spears, one young and goggling, one old and smirking, lean their heads together, mid-gossip. Pale cold light pours through the arch behind the rider and rakes the timber gate leaves with iron bosses; breath steams; townspeople in white hemp blur in the bright street beyond.

at: At his stirrup walks a junior warrior of twenty-four
alt: The dust-grey Western Commander rides in at walking pace; at his stirrup walks a young warrior with one wandering eye, leading the spare horses.
scene: Medium-wide side shot along the packed-earth road just inside Pyongyang’s gate, overcast winter noon breaking to one low shaft of sun. The Western Commander, the attached face, older, cautious, grey dust on his steel lamellar and his dark travelling cloak, rides a tired brown horse at a walk, eyes half-closed. At his stirrup walks the junior warrior, the second attached face but twenty-four: light stubble only, plain topknot, no helmet, undyed white hemp coat over a simple leather vest, leading two spare horses by the reins, one of his eyes looking forward and the other drifting aside. In the blurred foreground a kitchen maid with a basket and a water carrier with a yoke turn their heads to watch. Red Goguryeo pennants on the gate tower behind, granulated grey sky.

at: The South comes third, to drums.
alt: The Southern Commander rides in to drums while the king’s chamberlain bows at the gate to receive him and the crowd cranes to see.
scene: Worm’s-eye view from the gate steps of Pyongyang’s red two-tier munru, winter afternoon. The Southern Commander, the attached face, sharp and proud, in polished Goguryeo steel lamellar with red wing shoulder-cloth, rides a tall grey through the arch, one hand raised to the crowd, a rolled map tucked in his saddle. A palace chamberlain in long dark court silk and a black gauze cap bows low at his stirrup in the foreground, back to us. Drummers on the wall-top beat big barrel drums, sticks blurred. Onlookers in white hemp crowd the edges, faces up. One hard warm shaft of low sun through the arch catches the steel plates and the drum skins; red pennants snap in the wind.

at: Yeon comes last, in his father’s place
alt: Yeon arrives last at Pyongyang’s gate with Dosuryu; a palace steward, mistaking him for an aide, points him toward the yard.
scene: Over-the-shoulder shot from behind a palace steward in grey court silk and a black cap, his arm extended, pointing Yeon toward the side yard. Yeon Gesomun, twenty-nine, the attached face, on his red-bay horse in travel-stained Goguryeo steel lamellar and a dark cloak, red cloth at the collar, looks down at the steward with an unreadable stare that is almost a laugh. Beside him on foot, Dosuryu, the second attached face, older, scowling at the steward, the Eastern seal pouch on his belt. Behind, two gate guards squint and whisper. The red two-tier munru gate fills the background in winter haze; one low cold side-light rakes across Yeon’s face and the horse’s neck; long shadows on packed earth.

at: Yeon kicks the stone. On the long wall at home
alt: In the palace yard Yeon kicks a leaning stone in the horse wall and it does not move; the young western warrior watches with one eye, arms folded.
scene: Worm’s-eye view from the base of a low dry-stone tethering wall in a palace yard in Pyongyang, winter morning. A leaning grey top stone is huge in the foreground; Yeon Gesomun’s boot strikes it mid-kick, grit flying, the stone not moving at all. Above, his face is a wince he is trying to turn into anger; a plumb line dangles from his fist. No sword on him. To the right the junior warrior, the second attached face but twenty-four, stubble only, bare head with plain topknot, undyed white hemp coat, stands with arms folded, deadpan, one eye on Yeon and the other wandering off. Tethered horses blurred behind, a groom hiding a laugh. Low winter sun rakes the stone and throws long shadows; palace giwa roofs dissolve in haze.

at: The first pot of tea goes round by rank.
alt: In the antechamber three veteran commanders drink tea and bargain while Yeon, at the far end, pours his own cup.
scene: Low wide shot down a dim timber antechamber, a long low table receding from the lens, winter light from one lattice window at the far end. Three veteran Goguryeo commanders, the first, second and third attached faces, in dark court robes over lamellar, sit cross-legged nearest the light, leaning together, mid-bargain, one gesturing with a teacup, one laughing. At the near foot of the table, sharp in the foreground, Yeon Gesomun, the fourth attached face, pours his own tea from an empty-looking pot, jaw set, eyes up on them, ignored. A brazier glows beside him, his face lit warm from below and the side; steam from the cups catches the window shaft. Crow-stamped ring-pommel swords lie beside the veterans.

at: They share a surname and stand an arm’s length apart
alt: At the king’s inner door Gusesa, smiling mildly, and Yeon stand an arm’s length apart, kin by name and nothing else.
scene: Two-shot in profile at the inner door of the palace antechamber, a carved lattice door between them, half open, warm lamplight from the king’s side spilling through it onto the older man. Yeon Gusesa, the first attached face, the High Commander, in rich dark-green court silk and a tall black gauze cap, hands folded in his sleeves, smiles mildly, lit gold from the doorway. Yeon Gesomun, the second attached face, stands on the dark side in his steel lamellar and red collar cloth, chin up, unsmiling, cold window light on his face. Exactly an arm’s length of floor between them, the dark floorboards catching the gold seam of light. Shallow depth of field, a lamp flame sharp in the foreground corner.

at: Nobody asks the foot of the table anything.
alt: At the Summit table the king leans toward the Southern Commander; at the far foot of the table, unasked, Yeon drinks his second cup.
scene: Long lens down the length of the Summit table in a dark timber hall, the king on a low dais at the far end, crowned, leaning forward with interest toward the Southern Commander who sits nearest him, gesturing at a map on the table. Every other head turns to them. In the sharp near foreground, at the foot of the table, Yeon Gesomun sits alone and last, beside the clerk’s inkstone, a teacup at his lips, eyes over its rim fixed on the king. Crow-stamped ring-pommel swords lie on the table before each seat except his. One hard window shaft falls on the king and the South; Yeon is lit only by a small oil lamp at his elbow, warm from the side.

at: with a tilt you could see from the emperor’s tent
alt: On Ansi's battered wall the Guardian sets a stone at a deliberate tilt while a young archer frowns at it; the Tang earthen mountain rises beyond.
scene: Over-the-shoulder shot from behind a young archer on the inside of Ansi's stone wall during the siege, summer dusk. The Guardian of Ansi, the attached face, bearded, in steel Goguryeo lamellar with red wing shoulder-cloth, no helmet, kneels on the parapet and sets a heavy grey stone into the gap with both hands, deliberately tilted into the hill, his face calm, one eye looking at the stone and the other wandering. Beyond the wall rises the raw brown slope of the Tang earthen mountain, hauling baskets on it, smoke and yellow Tang banners in haze. Torches along the parapet throw warm bokeh; one low red-gold sun shaft through smoke lands on his hands and the stone.

alt: In a snowbound cave, Gulgul bends over his sleeping son by a tiny fire and speaks to the top of his head in Mohe.
scene: Close two-shot inside a narrow mountain cave in Manchuria, deep winter night. A fire the size of two cupped hands burns low on the stone floor in the foreground, sharp, with ember bokeh. The boy Dae Joyoung, about twelve, asleep curled against his father under heavy furs, both fists closed around a bundle of red silk with a glint of gold. Dae Gulgul, the attached grown face, weathered, thin moustache and short beard, heavy white-grey fur mantle over grey lamellar, bends his head to the top of the boy's head, eyes half closed, lips moving on a word, the hardest face softened for once. The coals light them from below; the cave mouth behind is a pale blue wall of falling snow. Rough rock walls angled to the lens, their two shadows climbing the stone.
